slides.title: Lecture to explore how group dynamics influence social change
slides.highlight: This lecture explores how group dynamics influence social change, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on group norms and social perception.

slides.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
slides.tldr: COPYING MODELS EXPLAIN COLLECTIVE AI AGENT BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how simple copying mechanisms drive the collective structure and steerability of AI agent populations, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Proportional copying explains the emergent collective coordination of AI agents interacting on a public wiki.
card.key_idea: Agents choose pages, usernames, and phrasing by copying options in proportion to their visibility in recent feeds and current pages, governed by a simple recency mechanism.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 13,661 edits from 3,099 handles; three minimal models with single free parameters successfully reproduced observed heavy-tailed distributions and convention patchworks.
card.limitation: The study relies on reconstructed visibility rather than logged attention, and the data depends on a specific, rare public record.

slides.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT REASONING FOR SPEAKER RELATIONSHIP INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-free multi-agent reasoning framework to infer speaker relationships from conversations, contributing to the social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A training-free multi-agent reasoning framework improves speaker relationship inference from multimodal conversational data.
card.key_idea: Introduces Multi-Role Multi-Agent Debate (assigning complementary social perspectives) and Multi-Agent Compete (pairwise adjudication tournament) to resolve ambiguous relational cues without task-specific training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Seamless Interaction dataset (text, audio, audio+text) against zero-shot and debate baselines. Results show improvements in macro F1 and accuracy.
card.limitation: Higher inference-time costs due to multiple LLM calls and limited generalization testing on a single benchmark dataset.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE DIALOGUE MANAGEMENT FOR GROUP-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to improve uncertainty-aware decision-making and interpretability in multi-party human-robot interactions, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian neural network for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It decomposes behavior selection into a multi-stage hierarchical process (addressee and dialogue act) using Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty-aware prediction and decision-tree surrogates for explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian models outperformed deterministic versions and state-of-the-art baselines.

slides.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: SocioGesture enables robots to recognize social cues like invitations and refusals in real-time, supporting the HRI goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: SocioGesture is a real-time, adaptive social gesture perception system for robust human-robot interaction on edge devices.
card.key_idea: A lightweight dual-stream body-hand skeleton model using occlusion-aware training and an uncertainty-driven offline adaptation loop for vocabulary expansion via cloud-based video labeling.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via LOSO cross-validation on a custom HRI dataset and live Unitree G1 trials; demonstrated high robustness to joint occlusion and real-time edge latency.
card.limitation: Cannot recover information from severe occlusions and relies on offline human verification for scalable, safe model adaptation.

slides.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion
slides.tldr: PIPELINE FOR FULL-DUPLEX SPEECH DATA GENERATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to reconstruct and expand real two-speaker conversations, preserving turn-taking, overlaps, and interruptions. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: ConversationalVoice transforms real two-speaker audio into separated, reconstructed, and expanded full-duplex speech training data.
card.key_idea: A three-stage pipeline: separation recovers original tracks; reconstruction resynthesizes clean audio preserving source timing; expansion generates new, context-grounded dialogue with explicit interaction planning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via WER, NISQA, DNSMOS, and Gemini-based judgments. Results show high speaker similarity (0.983–0.991) and strong contextual coherence (4.94/5).
card.limitation: Evaluation is entirely automatic; downstream gains in full-duplex model training have not yet been measured.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS. MACHINE INTERACTION PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research compares human social intuition with machine reasoning in predicting interaction intentions from a robot's perspective, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Humans significantly outperform VLMs and pose-based models in anticipating human-robot interactions from egocentric video.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking human intuition against lightweight pose models (LSTM, ST-GCN, SkateFormer) and various VLMs using pose-only and full egocentric video inputs to predict interaction intent.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 100 HUI360 test tracks using F1-score. Results show humans lead (F1 0.77) while VLMs struggle to integrate social and temporal cues.
card.limitation: VLMs often reduce the task to simple approach detection, failing to reason effectively over complex social and temporal dynamics.

slides.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.highlight: AV-STE uses a modular audio-visual front-end to restore corrupted speech tokens from noisy audio and lip video, enhancing response coherence in full-duplex dialogue. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and robust listener modeling in noisy environments.

card.one_liner: AV-STE enhances corrupted semantic speech tokens using lip video to improve frozen dialogue model robustness.
card.key_idea: A modular streaming front-end using a causal AV-HuBERT encoder and noise-adaptive fusion (cross-attention and entropy-based modulation) to restore semantic tokens before they reach a frozen LLM.
card.evaluation: Tested on LRS3 and Seamless Interaction datasets using semantic-token accuracy and GPT-4o coherence scores. Results show significant gains under severe noise (-10dB).
card.limitation: Sensitive to domain shift, assumes reliable visual input, and introduces slight representation mismatch on clean speech.
